content.title: About
content.content: Defatted soy flour is produced from soybeans after the oil has been removed. It is a light‑brown powder with a neutral taste, high in protein and fiber, and is widely used in cooking and the food industry as a wheat‑flour alternative.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Defatted soy flour contains about 50 % protein, making it an excellent source of plant protein.
It is naturally gluten‑free, suitable for gluten‑free diets.
Soy has been cultivated for over 5,000 years, making it one of the oldest crops.
Removing the fat increases protein concentration and lowers the calorie content compared with whole soy flour.
Soy flour is used to improve the texture of meat substitutes and in baked goods.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides roughly 50 g of high‑quality plant protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Defatting reduces calories, which can be helpful for weight management.

items.title: Contains isoflavones
items.content: Phytoestrogens in soy may support hormonal balance and act as antioxidants.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to soy may experience reactions ranging from mild to severe.

items.title: Phytoestrogen content
items.content: High intake of isoflavones can affect hormone levels; people with hormone‑sensitive conditions should consult a healthcare professional.

items.title: Anti‑nutrients
items.content: Soy contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soy flour can be used in breads, pancakes, breadings, vegetarian patties, and as a thickener for sauces and soups. It blends well with other gluten‑free flours to improve texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated or frozen to prevent oxidation.
